name: Cleopatra
hook: The last pharaoh, two Roman lovers, an asp, and Elizabeth Taylor's epic.

facts.label: the last pharaoh
facts.statement: Cleopatra was the last active pharaoh of Egypt; after her death in 30 B.C. Egypt became a Roman province.

facts.label: the asp
facts.statement: Cleopatra reportedly killed herself with an asp, the Egyptian cobra Shakespeare calls "the pretty worm of Nilus."

facts.label: Mark Antony
facts.statement: Mark Antony was her Roman lover; at Tarsus in 41 B.C. she arrived dressed as Aphrodite on a barge, and after his death their children were raised by Octavia.

facts.label: Julius Caesar
facts.statement: Julius Caesar was her lover and the father of her son Caesarion; Handel's opera Giulio Cesare sets the affair in Egypt.

facts.label: Ptolemy
facts.statement: Cleopatra married her brother Ptolemy XIII, then ruled with another brother, Ptolemy XIV, after XIII drowned in the Nile.

facts.label: Alexandria
facts.statement: Alexandria was her capital, and the sunken island of Antirhodos offshore was where she once lived. Both Cleopatra's Needles stood at the Caesareum, not on Antirhodos; they came originally from Heliopolis.

facts.label: the 1963 film Cleopatra
facts.statement: Elizabeth Taylor starred in the budget-busting 1963 epic Cleopatra, which Joseph Mankiewicz directed.
